Phyl (Lily Ganser, Stereophonic , in an impressive Off Broadway debut) is a spirited young governess in charge of two nasty children, Betty (Tessa Bilmes) and Olive (Charlotte Van Ledtje), daughters of the wealthy, imperious, straitlaced Mrs. Ponsonby (Katie Firth). Act One transpires in the schoolroom of her grand home.
Some of the period costumes delivered by Alicia J. Austin could be better tailored and finished.
More than a century after Phyl first provoked outrage, Hamilton’s story of a woman challenging the limits imposed on her remains thoroughly engaging.
This is an entertaining play with meat on it and an utterly captivating production.
Seldom do a production’s elements complement one another so effectively.
Phyl is powerfully relevant and magnificently presented.

Under the direction of Britt Berke, Phyl emerges as a charming, quietly rebellious comedy whose questions about women's independence remain surprisingly recognizable more than a century after it was written.

cn.t: Critics praise this Mint Theater rediscovery of Hamilton's 1913 feminist comedy for its bold, timely examination of women's limited options and Lily Ganser's spirited lead performance, though some note the writing shows its age.

vr.q: If you like realistic plays, if you want to discover a gem from a bygone era that still resonates today, if you want to see really great performance done by great actors, I found this incredibly enjoyable.
